items.stem: Explain why ∫ 1/x dx is written ln|x| + c rather than ln x + c.
items.answer: ln x is only defined for x > 0, but 1/x is defined for x < 0 too; d/dx ln|x| = 1/x for all x ≠ 0.

items.stem: Explain why ∫ e^(3x) dx = (1/3)e^(3x) + c by differentiating the answer.
items.answer: d/dx[(1/3)e^(3x)] = (1/3) × 3e^(3x) = e^(3x), by the chain rule.
items.markingKey: M1 differentiates using the chain rule; A1 shows the result is e^(3x) [2]

items.stem: Explain why ∫ sin²x dx is not equal to (1/3) sin³x + c.

items.stem: Explain how to integrate (sin x + cos x)².
items.answer: Expand to sin²x + 2 sin x cos x + cos²x = 1 + sin 2x, then integrate: x − (1/2) cos 2x + c.
items.markingKey: B1 expands and uses sin² + cos² = 1 and sin 2x; B1 x − (1/2) cos 2x + c [2]

items.stem: Aisha writes ∫ cos²x dx = (1/3)cos³x + c. Explain why this is wrong and find the correct integral.

items.stem: Tariq writes cos²x = (1 − cos 2x)/2 and hence ∫ cos²x dx = x/2 − (1/4) sin 2x + c. Explain the error and give the correct integral.

items.markingKey: B1 missing factor 1/5; B1 (1/5) ln 4 [2]

Mohammed writes ∫ e^(5x + 5) dx = e^(5x + 5)/(5x + 5) + c, treating it like a power of x. Explain the error and give the correct integral.
items.answer: The exponential is not a power xⁿ; d/dx e^(5x + 5) = 5e^(5x + 5), so ∫ e^(5x + 5) dx = (1/5)e^(5x + 5) + c.
items.markingKey: B1 power rule not applicable; B1 (1/5)e^(5x + 5) + c [2]

items.stem: Daniel writes ∫ 1/(3x + 9) dx = ln|3x + 9| + c. Explain the error and give the correct integral.
items.answer: Differentiating ln|3x + 9| gives 3/(3x + 9), so a factor 1/3 is needed: (1/3) ln|3x + 9| + c.
items.markingKey: B1 checks by differentiating (chain rule factor 3); B1 (1/3) ln|3x + 9| + c [2]

(b) Give the area of the region bounded by the curve y = f(x), the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = 2 correct to 3 significant figures. (c) Find ∫ 2 sec²3x dx.

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = eˣ + 1/x for x > 0. (a) Find ∫ f(x) dx. (b) Find the exact area of the region bounded by the curve y = f(x), the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = 2. (c) Give the area of the region bounded by the curve y = f(x), the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = 2 correct to 3 significant figures. (d) Find ∫ 3 sec²x dx.
items.answer: (a) eˣ + ln x + c (b) e² − e + ln 2 (c) 5.36 (d) 3 tan x + c
items.markingKey: (a) B1 eˣ; B1 ln x [2] (b) M1 substitutes limits; A1 e² − e + ln 2 [2] (c) B1 5.36 [1] (d) B1 3 tan x + c [1]

items.stem: Find ∫ 4 sin²x dx.
items.markingKey: Use the identity for sin²: ∫ = 4((1/2)x − (1/4) sin 2x) + c.

items.stem: Daniel writes ∫ tan²2x dx = (1/2) sec²2x + c. Explain the error and find the correct integral.
items.answer: tan²u = sec²u − 1, and it is sec²u that integrates to tan u. ∫ tan²2x dx = (1/2) tan 2x − x + c.
items.markingKey: B1 uses tan² = sec² − 1; B1 (1/2) tan 2x − x + c [2]

items.stem: Use the trapezium rule with 3 strips to estimate ∫_0.5^2.5 1/(1 + x²) dx, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Ines says that the trapezium rule estimate of ∫_0^1 x/(1 + eˣ) dx is an over-estimate. Using a sketch of y = x/(1 + eˣ) or its second derivative, explain whether Ines is right.
items.answer: Ines is wrong: the curve is concave downwards on [0, 1], so the chords lie below the curve and the rule gives an under-estimate.
items.markingKey: B1 concave downwards on the interval; B1 so under-estimate [2]
